prose.title: The Cilician Pirate Revolt
prose.summary: The Cilician coast rises and Nagidos and Korakesion become the Cilician Pirates. Both cities start the campaign in the hands of the Ptolemaic Empire. The revolt can break out early when one of the two rebels on its own, and it happens by itself at turn 102 (245 BC) at the latest.
prose.breaks_away_from: whoever holds Nagidos and Korakesion (at the start, the Ptolemaic Empire)
prose.who_it_can_happen_to: It can happen in any campaign, whether the two cities are held by a human or by the AI.
what_sets_it_off: Nagidos or Korakesion rebels on its own: the revolt then breaks out on a 25% chance, or for certain if Nagidos or Korakesion is already held by the Free Peoples.
If it has not happened before, the revolt breaks out automatically at the start of turn 102 (245 BC).
what_happens: Nagidos and Korakesion both rebel, whoever owns them, unless a city already belongs to the Cilician Pirates.
Both pass to the Cilician Pirates, a faction that does not exist at the start of the campaign.

Each city gets a garrison 3.5 times normal strength, drawn from Cilician Brigands, Kietaian Hillmen, Cilician Neocretan Archers, Cilician Pirates, Cilician Spearmen, Cilician Renowned Pirates and Cilician Cavalry.
The Cilician Pirates receive 10000 denarii when Nagidos joins them.
The revolt happens only once per campaign.
prose.playing_as_the_rebels: At the start of the turn after the revolt breaks out, by either route, the message 'Cilician Pirates Ravage Trade Routes!' offers the human player the chance to take over the Cilician Pirates, provided the player is playing the Seleucid Empire or the Ptolemaic Empire, or held Nagidos or Korakesion during the turn the revolt broke out. Accepting switches the player to the Cilician Pirates and adds a government building in Nagidos and Korakesion; declining changes nothing. Otherwise no offer is made. The Cilician Pirates are a playable faction.
